prop:li-wager-bridge.proof_tex:
Work throughout the finite-sample calculation conditionally on \(A\) and \((f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\), and define the proof-intermediate function
\[
 g_i(x):=\frac{f_i(1,x)+f_i(0,x)}2,
 \qquad x\in[0,1].
\]
By \({\rm ass:bernoulli-design}\), for every \(z\in\{0,1\}^{\mathcal V_n}\),
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{Z=z\mid A,(U_i,f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\right\}=2^{-n}.
\]
The displayed conditional probability is constant in the latent types.  Therefore the tower property gives
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{Z=z\mid A,(f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\right\}
 =\mathbb E\!\left[
   \Pr\!\left\{Z=z\mid A,(U_i,f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\right\}
   \mathrel{\big|}A,(f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}
 \right]
 =2^{-n}.
\]
Thus, under the conditional law appearing in \({\rm def:li-wager-target}\), the coordinates of \(Z\) are still independent \({\rm Bernoulli}(1/2)\) variables.

Fix \(i\in\mathcal V_n\) with \(N_i=m>0\).  Because \(A_{ii}=0\) under \({\rm ass:graphon-draw}\), the variable \(M_i\) depends only on \((Z_j)_{j\ne i}\).  The preceding product law and the definition of \(M_i\) consequently imply
\[
 M_i\sim {\rm Binomial}(m,1/2),
 \qquad Z_i\ \hbox{is independent of }M_i.
\]
Define
\[
 \beta_i:=4\,\mathbb E_Z\!\left[
 Y_i(Z)(M_i-m/2)\mid A,(f_j)_{j\in\mathcal V_n}
 \right].
\]
By \({\rm ass:anonymous-interference}\), \(Y_i(Z)=f_i(Z_i,1/2+V_i)\) for this positive-degree unit.  Averaging first over the independent variable \(Z_i\), and using \(M_i-m/2=mV_i\), yields
\[
 \beta_i
 =4m\,\mathbb E_Z\!\left[
 g_i(1/2+V_i)V_i\mid A,(f_j)_{j\in\mathcal V_n}
 \right].
\]
For \(N_i=0\), the factor \(M_i-N_i/2\) is zero, so put \(\beta_i=0\).  It follows directly from \({\rm def:li-wager-target}\) that
\[
 \bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}=\frac1n\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\beta_i.
\]

For the fixed positive-degree unit, let \(X_1,\ldots,X_m\) be independent variables taking values \(-1/2\) and \(1/2\), each with probability \(1/2\), and let \(S_m=\sum_{j=1}^mX_j\).  The binomial law identifies the conditional distribution of \(V_i\) with that of \(S_m/m\).  Centering, independence, and symmetry give
\[
 \mathbb E S_m=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E S_m^2=\sum_{j=1}^m\mathbb E X_j^2=\frac m4,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E S_m^3=0.
\]
In the fourth-power expansion, the only terms with nonzero expectation are the one-index terms and the terms formed from two index pairs.  Since \(\mathbb E X_j^2=1/4\) and \(\mathbb E X_j^4=1/16\),
\[
 \mathbb E S_m^4
 =\sum_{j=1}^m\mathbb E X_j^4
  +6\sum_{1\le j<k\le m}\mathbb E X_j^2\mathbb E X_k^2
 =\frac{3m^2-2m}{16}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \mathbb E V_i=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E V_i^2=\frac1{4m},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E V_i^3=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E V_i^4=\frac{3m^2-2m}{16m^4}\le\frac3{16m^2}.
\]

By \({\rm ass:third-derivative-bound}\) and the definition of \(g_i\),
\[
 \sup_{x\in[0,1]}|g_i^{(3)}(x)|\le L.
\]
Repeated use of the fundamental theorem of calculus on the segment from \(1/2\) to \(1/2+v\), which is contained in \([0,1]\) whenever \(|v|\le1/2\), gives
\[
 g_i(1/2+v)
 =g_i(1/2)+g_i'(1/2)v+\frac12g_i''(1/2)v^2+R_i(v),
\]
where
\[
 R_i(v)=\frac{v^3}{2}\int_0^1(1-t)^2g_i^{(3)}(1/2+tv)\,dt,
 \qquad
 |R_i(v)|\le\frac L6|v|^3.
\]
Multiplying the expansion by \(v\), taking conditional expectations, and using the four moment identities cancels the constant and quadratic terms, while \(4m\mathbb E V_i^2=1\).  Therefore
\[
 \beta_i-g_i'(1/2)
 =4m\,\mathbb E\!\left[V_iR_i(V_i)\mid A,(f_j)_{j\in\mathcal V_n}\right],
\]
and hence
\[
 |\beta_i-g_i'(1/2)|
 \le\frac{4mL}{6}\mathbb E V_i^4
 \le\frac{4mL}{6}\frac3{16m^2}
 =\frac{L}{8m}.
\]
By \({\rm def:target}\), the contribution of unit \(i\) to \(\theta_n\) is \(g_i'(1/2)\).  For an isolate, \({\rm ass:response-envelope}\) implies
\[
 |g_i'(1/2)|
 \le\frac{|\partial_xf_i(1,1/2)|+|\partial_xf_i(0,1/2)|}{2}
 \le B.
\]
Separating positive-degree units from isolates and applying the triangle inequality proves
\[
\begin{aligned}
 |\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}-\theta_n|
 &\le\frac1n\sum_{i:N_i>0}|\beta_i-g_i'(1/2)|
       +\frac1n\sum_{i:N_i=0}|g_i'(1/2)|\\
 &\le\frac{L}{8n}\sum_{i:N_i>0}\frac1{N_i}
       +\frac Bn\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}.
\end{aligned}
\]

We next prove the maintained-class center approximation using only the fixed lower-order envelope, so no uniform bound on \(L\) is needed along the sequence.  By \({\rm ass:response-envelope}\), \(\sup_x|g_i''(x)|\le B\).  Two integrations give
\[
 g_i(1/2+v)=g_i(1/2)+g_i'(1/2)v+T_i(v),
\]
where
\[
 T_i(v)=v^2\int_0^1(1-t)g_i''(1/2+tv)\,dt,
 \qquad
 |T_i(v)|\le\frac B2v^2.
\]
The same cancellations show
\[
 |\beta_i-g_i'(1/2)|\le2mB\,\mathbb E|V_i|^3.
\]
For completeness, the elementary nonnegativity relation
\[
 0\le\mathbb E\bigl[(|V_i|-tV_i^2)^2\bigr]
 =\mathbb EV_i^2-2t\mathbb E|V_i|^3+t^2\mathbb EV_i^4,
 \qquad t\in\mathbb R,
\]
implies, by the nonpositivity of the discriminant,
\[
 \mathbb E|V_i|^3\le
 \sqrt{\mathbb EV_i^2\,\mathbb EV_i^4}
 \le\frac{\sqrt3}{8m^{3/2}}.
\]
Thus the sharper bound
\[
 |\beta_i-g_i'(1/2)|\le\frac{\sqrt3 B}{4\sqrt m}
\]
holds for every \(m>0\).

Consider any maintained triangular-array sequence with fixed \(B\) and \(\kappa\) such that
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log(\rho_n)}{\log n}>-\frac12.
\]
There is an \(\varepsilon>0\) for which, eventually,
\[
 \rho_n\ge n^{-1/2+\varepsilon}.
\]
Fix \(i\).  By \({\rm ass:unit-sampling}\) and \({\rm ass:graphon-draw}\), conditional only on \(U_i=u\), the pairs formed by \(U_j\) and the edge draw \(A_{ij}\), for \(j\ne i\), are independent and identically distributed.  Integrating each \(U_j\) therefore gives
\[
 N_i\mid U_i=u\sim{\rm Binomial}(n-1,p_n(u)),
 \qquad
 p_n(u):=\rho_n\int_0^1W(u,v)\,dv.
\]
The conditions \({\rm ass:kernel-bound}\) and \({\rm ass:edge-probability}\) imply \(0\le p_n(u)\le\rho_n\kappa\le1\), and \({\rm ass:degree-regularity}\) gives, for almost every \(u\),
\[
 \mu_i(u):=\mathbb E[N_i\mid U_i=u]
 =(n-1)p_n(u)
 \ge\frac{(n-1)\rho_n}{\kappa}.
\]
Because the \(U_i\) have the uniform marginal specified in \({\rm ass:unit-sampling}\), the last almost-everywhere inequality holds for all of the finitely many sampled types with probability one at every \(n\).

We derive the only tail inequality needed below.  If \(S\sim{\rm Binomial}(m,p)\), \(\mu=mp\), and \(t=\log2\), then
\[
 \mathbf1\{S\le\mu/2\}\le e^{t(\mu/2-S)}.
\]
Independence of the Bernoulli summands and the elementary inequality \(1-y\le e^{-y}\) yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \Pr(S\le\mu/2)
 &\le e^{t\mu/2}\mathbb Ee^{-tS}
 =e^{t\mu/2}(1-p+pe^{-t})^m\\
 &\le\exp\!\left\{\frac{t\mu}{2}-\mu(1-e^{-t})\right\}
 =\exp\!\left\{-\frac{1-\log2}{2}\mu\right\}
 \le e^{-\mu/8},
\end{aligned}
\]
where the last step uses \((1-\log2)/2\ge1/8\).  Applying this inequality conditionally on each \(U_i\), integrating, and taking a union bound shows that
\[
 \mathcal E_n:=\left\{\min_{i\in\mathcal V_n}N_i
 \ge\frac{(n-1)\rho_n}{2\kappa}\right\}
\]
satisfies
\[
 \Pr(\mathcal E_n^c)
 \le n\exp\!\left\{-\frac{(n-1)\rho_n}{8\kappa}\right\}
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Indeed, \(n\rho_n\ge n^{1/2+\varepsilon}\) eventually, so the negative term in the exponent dominates \(\log n\).

On \(\mathcal E_n\), there are no isolates for all sufficiently large \(n\), and
\[
 \frac1n\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\frac1{\sqrt{N_i}}
 \le\left(\frac{2\kappa}{(n-1)\rho_n}\right)^{1/2}.
\]
The preceding lower-order bound therefore gives
\[
 \frac{|\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}-\theta_n|}{\sqrt{\rho_n}}
 \le\frac{\sqrt{6\kappa}\,B}{4\sqrt{n-1}\,\rho_n}
 \le\frac{\sqrt{6\kappa}\,B}{4\sqrt{1-1/n}\,n^\varepsilon}
 \longrightarrow0
 \qquad\hbox{on }\mathcal E_n.
\]
Together with \(\Pr(\mathcal E_n^c)\to0\), this proves
\[
 \bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}-\theta_n=o_P(\sqrt{\rho_n}).
\]

Finally, restrict the sequence to the intersection with every source hypothesis enumerated in \({\rm lem:li-wager-theorem-six-regime}\), and specialize the treatment probability to one half.  That cited lemma supplies the equation~(43) Gaussian limit centered at \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}\), with full standardizer \(\sqrt{\rho_n}\sigma_{\mathrm{IND},n}\).  Under the additional condition \(\liminf_n\sigma_{\mathrm{IND},n}>0\), there are constants \(c>0\) and \(n_0\) such that \(\sigma_{\mathrm{IND},n}\ge c\) for \(n\ge n_0\).  Consequently,
\[
 R_n:=\frac{\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}-\theta_n}
 {\sqrt{\rho_n}\sigma_{\mathrm{IND},n}}=o_P(1).
\]
Let \(T_n\) denote the equation~(43) statistic centered at \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}\).  The same statistic centered at \(\theta_n\) is exactly \(T_n+R_n\).  This additive limit step may be checked directly: for each \(x\in\mathbb R\) and \(\eta>0\),
\[
 \Pr(T_n\le x-\eta)-\Pr(|R_n|>\eta)
 \le\Pr(T_n+R_n\le x)
 \le\Pr(T_n\le x+\eta)+\Pr(|R_n|>\eta).
\]
The cited limit gives \(T_n\Rightarrow N(0,1)\), whereas the preceding display for \(R_n\) gives \(R_n=o_P(1)\).  Taking lower and upper limits and then letting \(\eta\downarrow0\), using continuity of the standard-normal distribution function, proves \(T_n+R_n\Rightarrow N(0,1)\).  This transfer uses every source condition and the stated full-standardizer nondegeneracy; it does not assert that every sequence in \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\) lies in the source theorem's class.  Moreover, the nonzero degree-exact remainder established above keeps \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}\) and \(\theta_n\) distinct rather than identifying them by definition.

snapshot.stmt:
Conditional on \(A\) and \((f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\), the derivative target and the Li--Wager finite indirect effect satisfy
\[
 \left|\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}-\theta_n\right|
 \le \frac{L}{8n}\sum_{i:N_i>0}\frac{1}{N_i}
 +\frac{B}{n}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf 1\{N_i=0\}.
\]
Moreover, along any maintained triangular-array sequence with fixed \(B\) and \(\kappa\) such that \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\log(\rho_n)/\log(n)>-1/2\), one has \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}-\theta_n=o_P(\sqrt{\rho_n})\). On the further intersection of such a sequence with every source hypothesis enumerated in \({\rm lem:li-wager-theorem-six-regime}\), specialize the treatment probability to one half and, writing \(\sigma_{\mathrm{IND},n}\) for the nonnegative variance factor in the full standardizer \(\sqrt{\rho_n}\sigma_{\mathrm{IND},n}\) of Li--Wager's equation~(43) at the \(n\)-th law, additionally suppose that \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\sigma_{\mathrm{IND},n}>0\). Then the equation~(43) Gaussian limit centered at \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}\) transfers by an additive Slutsky argument to the same statistic centered at \(\theta_n\). This is an asymptotic comparator only on that intersection, not a theorem for every sequence in \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\), and it is not a finite-sample equality of the two targets.

defs.def:li-wager-target: At Bernoulli probability one half, \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}=4n^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbb E_Z[Y_i(Z)(M_i-N_i/2)\mid A,(f_j)_{j\in\mathcal V_n}]\), equivalently the finite indirect effect in equation (1) of LiWager2022RandomGraph.

assumptions.ass:graphon-draw: Conditional on \((U_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\), the variables \((A_{ij})_{i<j}\) are independent with \(A_{ij}\sim{\rm Bernoulli}(\rho_nW(U_i,U_j))\), \(A_{ji}=A_{ij}\), and \(A_{ii}=0\).
assumptions.ass:unit-sampling: \((U_i,f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\) are independent and identically distributed preassignment draws from a joint law whose \(U_i\)-marginal is \({\rm Uniform}[0,1]\).

thm:honest-upper.proof_tex:
Put
\[
 a_\alpha=\sqrt{2\log(2/\alpha)}.
\tag{1}
\]
Because \(0<\alpha<1/2\), one has \(a_\alpha>1\).  Fix an index for which \(\mathcal H_{n,d}\ne\varnothing\).  By \({\rm def:bandwidth\text{-}set}\),
\[
 \mathcal H_{n,d}=[\ell,u],\quad
 \ell=d^{-1},\quad u=\min\{d^{-1/2},1/2\},
 \quad0<\ell\leq u\leq1/2.
\tag{2}
\]
For a fixed realized graph, list the distinct points of \(\mathcal K(A)\) as \(\ell=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_K=u\), with the single-point interpretation when \(\ell=u\).  Every score indicator has the form
\[
 \mathbf1\{|m/N_i-1/2|\leq\max(h,\delta_{N_i})\}.
\tag{3}
\]
Because the inequality is weak, all score-dependent terms are constant on each cell \([t_k,t_{k+1})\).  The matrix \(C_A\), the isolate term, and \(\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}\) are bandwidth independent, and \(\overline s_h(A)\) is constant on each cell.  The only varying term is
\[
 \frac{L}{6n}\sum_{i:N_i>0}\max\{h,\delta_{N_i}\}^2,
\tag{4}
\]
which is nondecreasing because \(L\geq0\).  Hence, for every \(h\in[t_k,t_{k+1})\),
\[
 \overline b_{t_k}(A)+\overline s_{t_k}(A)
 \leq\overline b_h(A)+\overline s_h(A).
\tag{5}
\]
The terminal point is itself a candidate.  Minimization over \(\mathcal K(A)\) proves the pointwise comparison
\[
 \overline b_{\widehat h(A)}(A)+\overline s_{\widehat h(A)}(A)
 \leq\overline b_h(A)+\overline s_h(A)
 \quad\text{for every }h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}.
\tag{6}
\]

Assume also that \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\ne\varnothing\), and define
\[
 J(h)=\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}
 \mathbb E_P[\overline b_h(A)+\overline s_h(A)].
\tag{7}
\]
Let
\[
 \mathcal K_n=\{\ell,u\}\cup
 \left\{\left|\frac mN-\frac12\right|:
 1\leq N\leq n-1,\ 0\leq m\leq N,\
 \ell\leq\left|\frac mN-\frac12\right|\leq u\right\}.
\tag{8}
\]
This deterministic set is finite and contains every possible graph-specific breakpoint.  Positive normalizers, the finite graph sample space, and the formulas in \({\rm def:radii}\) imply \(0\leq J(h)<\infty\).  Repeating (3)--(5) on the universal partition induced by \(\mathcal K_n\), then taking expectation and the supremum over the same nonempty class, gives
\[
 \inf_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}}J(h)=\min_{t\in\mathcal K_n}J(t).
\tag{9}
\]
Thus the smallest minimizer exists and is exactly \(h^\dagger\) in \({\rm def:exact\text{-}optimal\text{-}bandwidth}\).  It remains a class-level comparison object because (7) requires the full-class supremum.

Fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\) and set
\[
 \mathcal G=\sigma\!\left(A,(f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\right),
 \quad E_h=\widehat\theta_h-\theta_n,
 \quad m_h=\mathbb E_P(E_h\mid\mathcal G).
\tag{10}
\]
By \({\rm thm:explicit\text{-}pc\text{-}conditional\text{-}certificate}\),
\[
 |m_h|\leq\overline b_h(A),\quad
 \mathbb E_P[(E_h-m_h)^2\mid\mathcal G]\leq\overline s_h(A)^2,
\tag{11}
\]
and
\[
 \Pr_Z\{|E_h|\leq\overline b_h(A)+a_\alpha\overline s_h(A)\mid\mathcal G\}
 \geq1-\alpha.
\tag{12}
\]
The same theorem proves that \(\widehat h(A)\) is \(\mathcal G\)-measurable and assignment independent, so (11)--(12) remain valid at the selected bandwidth without a selection penalty.  Moreover, \({\rm ass:response\text{-}envelope}\) and \({\rm def:target}\) give
\[
 |\theta_n|\leq\frac1{2n}\sum_i
 \{ |\partial_xf_i(1,1/2)|+|\partial_xf_i(0,1/2)|\}\leq B.
\tag{13}
\]
For any \(h\), define
\[
 R_h(A)=\overline b_h(A)+a_\alpha\overline s_h(A),\quad
 L_h=\widehat\theta_h-R_h(A),\quad U_h=\widehat\theta_h+R_h(A),
\]
and let \(p(t)=\operatorname{clip}_{[-B,B]}(t)\).  Since \(R_h(A)\geq0\), one has \(L_h\leq U_h\).  The map \(p\) is nondecreasing, so \(p(L_h)\leq p(U_h)\), proving that the corrected \(\mathcal C_h=[p(L_h),p(U_h)]\) is a nonempty closed interval.  On the event in (12), \(L_h\leq\theta_n\leq U_h\); by (13), \(p(\theta_n)=\theta_n\), and hence
\[
 p(L_h)\leq\theta_n\leq p(U_h).
\tag{14}
\]
Thus endpoint clipping preserves the fixed and selected conditional coverage events.  The half-length of the unprojected interval \([L_h,U_h]\) is exactly \(R_h(A)\), including the explicit contributions of every positive degree and isolate in \({\rm def:radii}\).  Equation (2) also gives \(d^{-1}\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\).

Conditional Cauchy--Schwarz in (11), followed by the bias bound, gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P(|E_h|\mid\mathcal G)
 \leq\overline b_h(A)+\overline s_h(A).
\tag{15}
\]
Evaluate (15) at \(\widehat h(A)\), use (6) with \(h=h^\dagger\), and take expectations.  For every member law,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_P|\widehat\theta_{\widehat h(A)}-\theta_n|
 &\leq\mathbb E_P[\overline b_{\widehat h(A)}(A)+\overline s_{\widehat h(A)}(A)]\\
 &\leq\mathbb E_P[\overline b_{h^\dagger}(A)+\overline s_{h^\dagger}(A)].
\end{aligned}
\tag{16}
\]
Taking the supremum and using \({\rm def:frontier\text{-}envelope}\) proves
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}
 \mathbb E_P|\widehat\theta_{\widehat h(A)}-\theta_n|
 \leq\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}.
\tag{17}
\]
Integrating (14) proves
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}
 P\{\theta_n\in\mathcal C_{\widehat h(A)}\}\geq1-\alpha.
\tag{18}
\]

Finally, \(p\) is one-Lipschitz as the Euclidean projection onto \([-B,B]\).  Since its endpoints are ordered,
\[
 \operatorname{length}(\mathcal C_h)
 =p(U_h)-p(L_h)\leq U_h-L_h=2R_h(A).
\tag{19}
\]
Because \(a_\alpha>1\), (6) and (19) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{length}(\mathcal C_{\widehat h(A)})
 &\leq2\{\overline b_{\widehat h(A)}(A)+a_\alpha\overline s_{\widehat h(A)}(A)\}\\
 &\leq2a_\alpha\{\overline b_{\widehat h(A)}(A)+\overline s_{\widehat h(A)}(A)\}\\
 &\leq2a_\alpha\{\overline b_{h^\dagger}(A)+\overline s_{h^\dagger}(A)\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{20}
\]
Expectations, the class supremum, and (1) yield
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}
 \mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(\mathcal C_{\widehat h(A)})]
 \leq2\sqrt{2\log(2/\alpha)}\,\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}.
\tag{21}
\]
The operational conclusions come from (6), not from identifying \(\widehat h(A)\) with \(h^\dagger\), and the selected rule minimizes \(\overline b_h+\overline s_h\), not the literal exponential half-length.  No step compares \(\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}\) with \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\).

snapshot.stmt:
At every index for which \(\mathcal H_{n,d}\ne\varnothing\), the graph-observable selector \(\widehat h(A)\) is well defined, Borel measurable, and polynomial-time computable.  For every prespecified \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\) and every \(P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\), the feasible estimator and interval satisfy
\[
 \Pr_Z\{\theta_n\in\mathcal C_h\mid A,(f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\}\geq1-\alpha
\]
for almost every preassignment realization, and the same conditional guarantee holds after the graph-adaptive choice \(h=\widehat h(A)\).  Before endpoint clipping to \([-B,B]\), the pointwise half-length is exactly
\[
 \overline b_h(A)+\overline s_h(A)\sqrt{2\log(2/\alpha)},
\]
including every realized degree and isolate.  In particular, \(h=d^{-1}\) is admissible whenever \(\mathcal H_{n,d}\ne\varnothing\), while \(\widehat h(A)\) is the operational certificate-minimizing choice.

At every index for which both \(\mathcal H_{n,d}\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\ne\varnothing\), the class-level oracle bandwidth \(h^\dagger\) is well defined and is used only as a comparison object.  The pointwise candidate inequality implies the operational integrated bounds
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}
 \mathbb E_P|\widehat\theta_{\widehat h(A)}-\theta_n|
 \leq\mathfrak u_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}
 P\{\theta_n\in\mathcal C_{\widehat h(A)}\}\geq1-\alpha,
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}
 \mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(\mathcal C_{\widehat h(A)})]
 \leq2\sqrt{2\log(2/\alpha)}\,\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}.
\]
No comparison \(\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}\lesssim\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\), sharp minimax rate, or achieved honest expected-length frontier is asserted.

defs.def:estimator:
With the explicit score from \({\rm def:pc-handle}\),
\[
 \widehat\theta_h
 =\frac1n\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}
 \left[q_{i,h}-4\left\{\widehat\Pi_r(A)A
       (Z-\tfrac12\mathbf1_n)\right\}_i\right]Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}.
\]
defs.def:exact-optimal-bandwidth:
At every index for which \(\mathcal H_{n,d}\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\ne\varnothing\), define
\[
 h^\dagger=\min\operatorname*{argmin}_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}
 \mathbb E_P[\overline b_h(A)+\overline s_h(A)].
\]
This is the oracle full-class radius-minimizing bandwidth.  Its evaluation requires the full-class supremum and is not an operational data-driven tuning rule.
defs.def:honest-interval:
Put
\[
 a_\alpha=\sqrt{2\log(2/\alpha)},\qquad
 R_h(A)=\overline b_h(A)+a_\alpha\overline s_h(A),
\]
\[
 L_h=\widehat\theta_h-R_h(A),\qquad
 U_h=\widehat\theta_h+R_h(A),\qquad
 \operatorname{clip}_{[-B,B]}(t)=\max\{-B,\min\{B,t\}\}.
\]
Define the unprojected interval \(\mathcal J_h=[L_h,U_h]\) and the reported interval
\[
 \mathcal C_h=
 [\operatorname{clip}_{[-B,B]}(L_h),
  \operatorname{clip}_{[-B,B]}(U_h)].
\]
Thus \(\mathcal C_h\) is the endpointwise monotone projection of \(\mathcal J_h\) onto the known parameter range.
defs.def:model-class: \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}=\{P_{n,d,L}:\text{ every condition in the displayed member-property list holds for }P_{n,d,L}\text{ at triangular-array index }n\}\).  This is the maintained bounded, row-regular, known-rank, two-radius graphon class selected by exactly those properties.  It is neither identified with nor contained in the full Theorem~4/6 regime of LiWager2022RandomGraph; only the intersection of the two regimes is used for comparison.  In particular, \(C_{\log}\log n\leq d\) and \(d/n\to0\) do not imply the source condition \(-1/2<\liminf_n\log(\rho_n)/\log n\), and the displayed member properties do not reproduce every source condition.
defs.def:operational-bandwidth:
At every index for which \(\mathcal H_{n,d}\ne\varnothing\), put \(\ell=d^{-1}\), \(u=\min\{d^{-1/2},1/2\}\), and, for each realized graph \(A\), define the finite nonempty candidate set
\[
 \mathcal K(A)=\{\ell,u\}\cup
 \left\{\left|\frac m{N_i}-\frac12\right|:
 i\in\mathcal V_n,\ N_i>0,\ 0\leq m\leq N_i,\
 \ell\leq\left|\frac m{N_i}-\frac12\right|\leq u\right\}.
\]
The graph-adaptive operational bandwidth is
\[
 \widehat h(A)=\min\operatorname*{argmin}_{h\in\mathcal K(A)}
 \{\overline b_h(A)+\overline s_h(A)\}.
\]
All ties are therefore resolved deterministically toward the smallest candidate.  The construction uses only the observed graph, the known constants, and the finite-lattice certificates; it does not use \(Z\) or the observed outcomes.
defs.def:radii:
For the explicit certificates in \({\rm def:pc-handle}\), set
\[
 \overline b_h(A)=\frac{L}{6n}\sum_{i:N_i>0}h_i(h)^2
 +\frac{B}{n}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}
 +\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}
\]
and
\[
 \overline s_h(A)^2=\widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h}.
\]
Thus \(\overline s_h(A)\) is a finite-sample conditional standard-deviation certificate, not an asserted sharp-rate formula.

assumptions.ass:unit-sampling: \((U_i,f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\) are independent and identically distributed preassignment draws from a joint law whose \(U_i\)-marginal is \({\rm Uniform}[0,1]\).
assumptions.ass:graphon-draw: Conditional on \((U_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\), the variables \((A_{ij})_{i<j}\) are independent with \(A_{ij}\sim{\rm Bernoulli}(\rho_nW(U_i,U_j))\), \(A_{ji}=A_{ij}\), and \(A_{ii}=0\).
assumptions.ass:eigenfunction-bernstein: Each \(\psi_k(U_i)\) satisfies Bernstein's moment condition with parameter \(b_\psi\) for \(1\le k\le r\).

thm:minimax-lower.proof_tex:
Define \(\lambda_k=c_0/r\).  Because the intervals \(I_1,\ldots,I_r\) partition \([0,1]\) up to endpoints of Lebesgue measure zero,
\[
 \sum_{k=1}^r\lambda_k\psi_k(u)\psi_k(v)
 =c_0\mathbf1\{u\text{ and }v\text{ belong to the same }I_k\}
 =W_0(u,v)
\tag{1}
\]
for almost every \((u,v)\).  Moreover,
\[
 \int_0^1\psi_k(u)\psi_\ell(u)\,du=\mathbf1\{k=\ell\}.
\tag{2}
\]
All \(r\) eigenvalues in (1) are nonzero, and the definition of \(c_0\) gives
\[
 |\lambda_k|=c_0/r\geq\underline\lambda,\qquad
 \int_0^1W_0(u,v)\,dv=c_0/r\geq\kappa^{-1}.
\tag{3}
\]
The compatibility condition \(c_0\leq\kappa\) gives \(0\leq W_0\leq\kappa\).  Together with \({\rm ass:edge\text{-}probability}\), this makes every edge probability \(\rho_nW_0(U_i,U_j)\) lie in \([0,1]\).

To verify the Bernstein member property, note that
\[
 \overline\psi_k:=\int_0^1\psi_k(u)\,du=1/\sqrt r.
\]
For \(r\geq2\), the centered variable \(X_k=\psi_k(U)-\overline\psi_k\) takes the values \((r-1)/\sqrt r\) and \(-1/\sqrt r\), and hence \(|X_k|\leq(r-1)/\sqrt r\leq b_\psi\).  For every integer \(m\geq2\),
\[
 \mathbb E|X_k|^m
 \leq b_\psi^{m-2}\mathbb EX_k^2
 \leq\frac{m!}{2}b_\psi^{m-2}\mathbb EX_k^2.
\tag{4}
\]
For \(r=1\), \(X_k=0\), so (4) is immediate.  Thus the declared Bernstein moment condition holds.  Equations (1)--(4), the independent uniform latent types, \({\rm ass:graphon\text{-}draw}\), and \({\rm ass:bernoulli\text{-}design}\) establish the advertised known-rank equal-block graph submodel, including rank, positivity, degree regularity, spectral strength, and treatment overlap.

Put \(s_0=B/4\).  The function
\[
 p_{s_0}(t)=s_0^{-1}\cos^2\!\left(\frac{\pi t}{2s_0}\right)
 \mathbf1\{|t|\leq s_0\}
\tag{5}
\]
is nonnegative, is supported on \([-B/4,B/4]\), and integrates to one because the change of variables \(y=t/s_0\) gives
\[
 \int_{-s_0}^{s_0}p_{s_0}(t)\,dt
 =\int_{-1}^{1}\cos^2(\pi y/2)\,dy=1.
\tag{6}
\]
Let \(\xi_i\) be independent draws from this density, independent of the graph primitives.  For a deterministic function \(g\), define
\[
 f_i^\sigma(a,x)=\xi_i+\sigma g(x),\qquad \sigma\in\{-1,1\}.
\tag{7}
\]
The resulting \((U_i,f_i^\sigma)\) are independent and identically distributed.  Since \(g\) is independent of \(a\), \({\rm def:target}\) gives
\[
 \theta_n^\sigma=\sigma g'(1/2).
\tag{8}
\]

We now specialize the explicit response experiments proved in \({\rm thm:unrestricted\text{-}supported\text{-}converse}\) to the graphon \(W_0\).  Write
\[
 \phi(t)=t(1-t^2)^4\mathbf1\{|t|\leq1\}.
\tag{9}
\]
Its zero extension is \(C^3\), because the polynomial has a zero of order four at each endpoint, and \(\phi'(0)=1\).  For \(K_j=\sup_t|\phi^{(j)}(t)|\), choose fixed \(\gamma>0\) such that \(\gamma K_3\leq1\) and sufficiently small for the testing bounds below.  The three functions are
\[
\begin{aligned}
 g_G(x)&=a_G(x-1/2),
 &a_G&=\zeta s_0\sqrt{d/n},\\
 g_I(x)&=\gamma Lh_0^3\phi((x-1/2)/h_0),&&\\
 g_L(x)&=\gamma Lh_L^3\phi((x-1/2)/h_L),
 &h_L&=(4Kd)^{-1},
\end{aligned}
\tag{10}
\]
where \(\zeta>0\) is a sufficiently small fixed constant and \(K>\kappa\) is fixed and chosen so that
\[
 C_{\log}\{K\log(K/\kappa)-K+\kappa\}\geq4.
\tag{11}
\]
The interior function \(g_I\) is used only when \(L>0\) and \(d^{-1}<h_0<d^{-1/2}\); when \(L=0\), only the graph pair is needed.

We verify that (7) stays in the same response class.  For \(g_G\), \(d/n\to0\) implies eventually
\[
 \|g_G\|_\infty\leq B-s_0,\qquad |g_G'|=a_G\leq B,\qquad
 g_G''=g_G'''=0.
\tag{12}
\]
For either local bump \(g(x)=\gamma Lh^3\phi((x-1/2)/h)\), differentiation gives
\[
 \|g^{(j)}\|_\infty\leq\gamma Lh^{3-j}K_j,\qquad 0\leq j\leq3.
\tag{13}
\]
In the interior regime, \(h_0<d^{-1/2}\to0\); for the lattice bump, \(h_L\to0\).  Hence (13), \(\gamma K_3\leq1\), and fixed \(B,L\) imply, for all large \(n\),
\[
 \|g\|_\infty\leq B-s_0,\qquad
 \max_{1\leq j\leq2}\|g^{(j)}\|_\infty\leq B,\qquad
 \|g'''\|_\infty\leq L.
\tag{14}
\]
Equations (5), (7), (12), and (14) verify the response envelope and the third-derivative radius.  Thus every pair in (10), with the retained \(W_0\) graph law, belongs to \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).

For clarity, we recall the quantitative two-point conclusion established in \({\rm thm:unrestricted\text{-}supported\text{-}converse}\).  If \(P_g^+\) and \(P_g^-\) denote the two full observed-data laws generated by (7), its Hellinger calculation gives
\[
 H^2(P_g^+,P_g^-)
 \leq\frac{\pi^2}{s_0^2}\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbb E[g(T_i)^2],
\tag{15}
\]
where \(T_i=M_i/N_i\) for \(N_i>0\) and \(T_i=0\) for isolates.  Put \(\eta=(1-2\alpha)/2\in(0,1)\).  Whenever the right side of (15) is at most \(\eta^2\), total variation is at most \(\eta\), and the testing inequalities proved there yield, with \(a=|g'(1/2)|\),
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\theta}\max_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}}
 \mathbb E_{P_g^\sigma}|\widetilde\theta-\theta_n^\sigma|
 \geq\frac a2(1-\eta),
\tag{16}
\]
and, for every interval having coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) under both laws,
\[
 \max_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}}
 \mathbb E_{P_g^\sigma}[\operatorname{length}(\mathcal C)]
 \geq a(1-2\alpha).
\tag{17}
\]
These are internal proved consequences of the declared converse theorem, not additional assumptions.

For the block graphon, conditional degrees have means bounded above and below by fixed multiples of \(d\).  The moment calculation in \({\rm thm:unrestricted\text{-}supported\text{-}converse}\) therefore gives
\[
 \mathbb E(T_i-1/2)^2\leq C_1/d.
\tag{18}
\]
Equations (10), (15), and (18) show
\[
 H^2(P_{g_G}^+,P_{g_G}^-)
 \leq C_2\zeta^2.
\tag{19}
\]
Choosing \(\zeta\) once so that (19) is at most \(\eta^2\), equations (8), (10), and (16)--(17) give lower bounds of order \(\sqrt{d/n}\) for both criteria.

The binomial small-ball calculation in the declared converse theorem gives, uniformly for \(d^{-1}\leq h\leq d^{-1/2}\),
\[
 \Pr\{|T_i-1/2|\leq h\}\leq C_3h\sqrt d.
\tag{20}
\]
Since \(nL^2h_0^7\sqrt d=1\), equations (10), (15), and (20) imply
\[
 H^2(P_{g_I}^+,P_{g_I}^-)
 \leq C_4\gamma^2,\qquad
 |g_I'(1/2)|=\gamma Lh_0^2
 =\gamma L^{3/7}(n^2d)^{-1/7}.
\tag{21}
\]
Choose \(\gamma\) small enough that the first quantity in (21) is at most \(\eta^2\).  Equations (16)--(17) then give the interior lower term for both criteria.

For the lattice bump, every nonzero centered exposure-lattice point of a unit with \(1\leq N_i\leq Kd\) has absolute value at least \((2N_i)^{-1}\geq(2Kd)^{-1}>h_L\), while \(g_L(1/2)=0\).  Thus \(g_L(T_i)=0\) for these units and also for isolates.  The binomial Chernoff calculation in the declared converse theorem and (11) give
\[
 \Pr(N_i>Kd)\leq n^{-4}.
\tag{22}
\]
Consequently,
\[
 H^2(P_{g_L}^+,P_{g_L}^-)
 \leq C_5nL^2d^{-6}n^{-4}=o(1),\qquad
 |g_L'(1/2)|=\gamma Lh_L^2
 =\frac{\gamma L}{16K^2d^2}.
\tag{23}
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), equations (16)--(17) give the degree-lattice lower term \(Ld^{-2}\).  This pair agrees exactly on every vertex of degree at most \(Kd\); only the uniformly negligible upper-degree tail contributes to (23).

It remains to compare the three separations with the analytic envelope.  Put \(c_{n,d}=n^{-1/2}d^{-1/4}\) and \(g_0(h)=Lh^2+c_{n,d}h^{-3/2}\).  For \(L>0\),
\[
 Lh_0^2=c_{n,d}h_0^{-3/2}.
\tag{24}
\]
At all large indices, \(\mathcal H_{n,d}=[d^{-1},d^{-1/2}]\).  Evaluation at the appropriate endpoint or at \(h_0\) gives
\[
 \inf_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}}g_0(h)
 \leq
 \begin{cases}
 2Ld^{-2},&h_0\leq d^{-1},\\
 2Lh_0^2,&d^{-1}<h_0<d^{-1/2},\\
 2\sqrt{d/n},&h_0\geq d^{-1/2}.
 \end{cases}
\tag{25}
\]
For \(L=0\), evaluation at \(d^{-1/2}\) gives the last order directly.  By \({\rm def:frontier\text{-}envelope}\), \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}=\sqrt{d/n}+\inf_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}}g_0(h)\).  The largest applicable separation in (19), (21), and (23) is therefore at least a fixed multiple of \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\), because the maximum of two nonnegative quantities is at least half their sum.  Since all testing laws are in the explicit block submodel, equations (16)--(17) and \({\rm def:minimax\text{-}criteria}\) yield
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}
\tag{26}
\]
eventually, where \(c>0\) depends only on the fixed class constants and \(\alpha\), not on \(n,d\).  The compatibility inequalities were used only to certify the convenient block witness through (3)--(4).  Independently, \({\rm thm:unrestricted\text{-}supported\text{-}converse}\) proves (26) by retaining the graph primitives of any admissible member, so these sufficient block inequalities do not characterize nonemptiness of the maintained class.

snapshot.stmt:
For \(1\leq k\leq r\), let \(I_k=[(k-1)/r,k/r)\), with \(1\) included in \(I_r\), put \(\psi_k(u)=\sqrt r\,\mathbf 1\{u\in I_k\}\), and set
\[
 c_0=\max\{r/\kappa,r\underline\lambda\},
 \qquad
 W_0(u,v)=c_0\mathbf 1\{u\text{ and }v\text{ belong to the same }I_k\}.
\]
Suppose, in addition to the conditions defining \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\), that
\[
 c_0\leq\kappa,
 \qquad
 b_\psi\geq (r-1)/\sqrt r.
\]
Let \(s_0=B/4\), let \(\xi_i\) be i.i.d. with density \(p_{s_0}(t)=s_0^{-1}\cos^2(\pi t/(2s_0))\mathbf 1\{|t|\leq s_0\}\), and use response pairs \(f_i^\pm(a,x)=\xi_i\pm g(x)\), with the three functions \(g\) constructed in the proof.  Then \(W_0\) and these random-intercept response laws generate an explicit block submodel of \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\).  Along sequences with \(B,L,r,\kappa,\underline\lambda,b_\psi,\alpha,C_{\log}\) fixed and \(C_{\log}\log n\leq d=o(n)\), there is a constant \(c>0\), independent of \(n\) and \(d\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}.
\]
Within this same block submodel, respectively, a degree-lattice bump, an interior \(C^3\) bump, and a linear response pair furnish the lattice term, the interior nonlinear term for both absolute risk and honest expected length, and the graph floor.  The two displayed compatibility inequalities are only sufficient conditions for this explicit block witness and do not characterize nonemptiness; \({\rm thm:unrestricted\text{-}supported\text{-}converse}\) separately proves the same supported lower benchmark over every eventually nonempty repaired class.

defs.def:lattice-radius: For \(N\ge1\), set \(\delta_N=N^{-1}\) when \(N\) is even and \(\delta_N=(2N)^{-1}\) when \(N\) is odd; for each \(i\) with \(N_i>0\), set \(h_i(h)=\max\{h,\delta_{N_i}\}\).
defs.def:minimax-criteria: At every index for which \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\ne\varnothing\), let \(D=(A,Z,(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}})_{i\in\mathcal V_n})\). Define \(R^*_{n,d,L}=\inf_{\widetilde\theta}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}\mathbb E_P|\widetilde\theta-\theta_n|\), where the infimum ranges over all real-valued measurable estimators \(\widetilde\theta=\widetilde\theta(D)\). Define \(\Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)=\inf_{\mathcal C}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}\mathbb E_P[u(D)-\ell(D)]\), where the infimum ranges over data-measurable closed intervals \(\mathcal C(D)=[\ell(D),u(D)]\) with finite measurable endpoints \(\ell(D)\leq u(D)\) and satisfying \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}P\{\theta_n\in\mathcal C(D)\}\geq1-\alpha\). For every such interval, \(\operatorname{length}\{\mathcal C(D)\}=u(D)-\ell(D)\).
defs.def:model-class: \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}=\{P_{n,d,L}:\text{ every condition in the displayed member-property list holds for }P_{n,d,L}\text{ at triangular-array index }n\}\).  This is the maintained bounded, row-regular, known-rank, two-radius graphon class selected by exactly those properties.  It is neither identified with nor contained in the full Theorem~4/6 regime of LiWager2022RandomGraph; only the intersection of the two regimes is used for comparison.  In particular, \(C_{\log}\log n\leq d\) and \(d/n\to0\) do not imply the source condition \(-1/2<\liminf_n\log(\rho_n)/\log n\), and the displayed member properties do not reproduce every source condition.

assumptions.ass:eigenfunction-bernstein: Each \(\psi_k(U_i)\) satisfies Bernstein's moment condition with parameter \(b_\psi\) for \(1\le k\le r\).
assumptions.ass:graphon-draw: Conditional on \((U_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\), the variables \((A_{ij})_{i<j}\) are independent with \(A_{ij}\sim{\rm Bernoulli}(\rho_nW(U_i,U_j))\), \(A_{ji}=A_{ij}\), and \(A_{ii}=0\).
assumptions.ass:unit-sampling: \((U_i,f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\) are independent and identically distributed preassignment draws from a joint law whose \(U_i\)-marginal is \({\rm Uniform}[0,1]\).

prop:phase-diagram.proof_tex:
Assume \(L>0\), and put
\[
 c_{n,d}=n^{-1/2}d^{-1/4},\qquad
 g(h)=Lh^2+c_{n,d}h^{-3/2},\qquad
 \ell=d^{-1},\qquad u=d^{-1/2}.
\tag{1}
\]
By \({\rm ass:log\text{-}degree}\), \(d\to\infty\) along the triangular array.  Thus \(d\geq4\) eventually, and \({\rm def:bandwidth\text{-}set}\) gives \(\mathcal H_{n,d}=[\ell,u]\).  From \({\rm def:optimal\text{-}bandwidth}\),
\[
 h_0^7=\frac{L^{-2}}{n\sqrt d}.
\tag{2}
\]
Since \(c_{n,d}^2=(n\sqrt d)^{-1}\), positivity and (2) imply
\[
 Lh_0^2=c_{n,d}h_0^{-3/2}.
\tag{3}
\]
If \(h_0\leq\ell\), then \(g(h)\geq L\ell^2\) for every admissible \(h\), whereas
\[
 c_{n,d}\ell^{-3/2}
 \leq c_{n,d}h_0^{-3/2}
 =Lh_0^2\leq L\ell^2.
\]
Evaluation at \(\ell\) gives
\[
 Ld^{-2}\leq\inf_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}}g(h)\leq2Ld^{-2}.
\tag{4}
\]
If \(\ell<h_0<u\), then for \(h\geq h_0\), \(Lh^2\geq Lh_0^2\), while for \(h\leq h_0\), \(c_{n,d}h^{-3/2}\geq c_{n,d}h_0^{-3/2}=Lh_0^2\).  Evaluation at \(h_0\) gives
\[
 Lh_0^2\leq\inf_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}}g(h)\leq2Lh_0^2,
 \qquad
 Lh_0^2=L^{3/7}(n^2d)^{-1/7}.
\tag{5}
\]
If \(h_0\geq u\), then every admissible \(h\) satisfies \(g(h)\geq c_{n,d}u^{-3/2}=\sqrt{d/n}\), while
\[
 Lu^2\leq Lh_0^2=c_{n,d}h_0^{-3/2}
 \leq c_{n,d}u^{-3/2}.
\]
Evaluation at \(u\) proves
\[
 \sqrt{d/n}\leq\inf_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}}g(h)
 \leq2\sqrt{d/n}.
\tag{6}
\]
Combining (4)--(6) with
\[
 \mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}
 =\sqrt{d/n}+\inf_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}}g(h)
\tag{7}
\]
proves all three asserted equivalences, with constants independent of \(n,d\).

Fix an index at which both \(\mathcal H_{n,d}\) and \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\) are nonempty.  By \({\rm thm:honest\text{-}upper}\), the observed-data estimator \(\widehat\theta_{\widehat h(A)}\) satisfies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}
 \mathbb E_P|\widehat\theta_{\widehat h(A)}-\theta_n|
 \leq\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}.
\tag{8}
\]
It is an admissible competitor in \({\rm def:minimax\text{-}criteria}\), hence
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\leq\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}.
\tag{9}
\]
The same theorem states that the endpoint-clipped interval \(\mathcal C_{\widehat h(A)}\) is a data-measurable nonempty closed interval, is uniformly honest after integration, and obeys
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}
 \mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(\mathcal C_{\widehat h(A)})]
 \leq2\sqrt{2\log(2/\alpha)}\,\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}.
\tag{10}
\]
It is therefore an admissible interval competitor in \({\rm def:minimax\text{-}criteria}\), so
\[
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)
 \leq2\sqrt{2\log(2/\alpha)}\,\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}.
\tag{11}
\]

Along every sequence covered by \({\rm thm:unrestricted\text{-}supported\text{-}converse}\), that theorem supplies a constant \(c>0\), independent of \(n,d\), such that eventually
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)
 \geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}.
\tag{12}
\]
Under the two compatibility inequalities in \({\rm thm:minimax\text{-}lower}\), its explicit block response pairs are members of the maintained class, so their lower bounds transfer upward to that class.  The unrestricted theorem proves (12) directly without the block compatibility conditions.  By the nonnesting qualification in \({\rm def:model\text{-}class}\), and because \(\theta_n\) differs from the finite indirect-effect target in LiWager2022RandomGraph, neither argument transfers automatically to that source regime.

Finally, \({\rm thm:conditional\text{-}isolate\text{-}wall}\) gives, on every realized graph,
\[
 b(A)\geq\frac Bn\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}
\tag{13}
\]
for every uniformly valid graph-only conditional-bias certificate of the stated kind.  Equations (9), (11), and (12) are the conservative lower--upper bracket.  Its lower side is \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\), whereas its upper side is \(\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}\).  No declared result bounds the latter by the former, so (4)--(7) describe tuning geometry and a lower benchmark, not a sharp minimax rate or an achieved honest expected-length frontier.

snapshot.stmt:
For \(L>0\), at every sufficiently large triangular-array index the supported-unit component satisfies \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\asymp Ld^{-2}+\sqrt{d/n}\) when \(h_0\leq d^{-1}\), \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\asymp L^{3/7}(n^2d)^{-1/7}+\sqrt{d/n}\) when \(d^{-1}<h_0<d^{-1/2}\), and \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\asymp\sqrt{d/n}\) when \(h_0\geq d^{-1/2}\).  At every index for which \(\mathcal H_{n,d}\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\ne\varnothing\), the operational graph-adaptive selector satisfies
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\leq\mathfrak u_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)
 \leq2\sqrt{2\log(2/\alpha)}\,\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}.
\]
Along every sequence covered by the unrestricted supported converse, there is a constant \(c>0\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}.
\]
Every graph-only conditional-bias certificate over the maintained class retains at least \(Bn^{-1}\sum_i\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}\) on a realized graph.  The explicit compatible block-submodel lower bound transfers upward only to the maintained class, and the unrestricted converse proves the maintained-class lower benchmark directly; neither result transfers automatically to the nonnested LiWager2022RandomGraph Theorem~6 regime or its distinct finite indirect-effect target.  No bound \(\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}\lesssim\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\) is proved, so the three analytic phases remain tuning geometry and a minimax lower benchmark rather than a sharp or achieved frontier.

defs.def:empirical-projector:
Put \(m_{r,n}=\min\{r,n\}\).  Order the \(n\) eigenvalues of the symmetric matrix \(A\) by decreasing absolute value, breaking equal-absolute-value ties by decreasing signed value.  Within every remaining repeated eigenspace, choose the orthonormal basis obtained by applying Gram--Schmidt to the nonzero vectors in the ordered list of projections of \(e_1,\ldots,e_n\) onto that eigenspace.  Let \(\widehat\Psi_r(A)\in\mathbb R^{n\times m_{r,n}}\) contain the first \(m_{r,n}\) resulting orthonormal eigenvectors and define
\[
 \widehat\Pi_r(A)=\widehat\Psi_r(A)\widehat\Psi_r(A)^\top.
\]
Thus \(\widehat\Pi_r(A)\) is the orthogonal spectral projector onto the leading \(\min\{r,n\}\)-dimensional eigenspace selected by this convention.  The deterministic tie rule makes \(A\mapsto\widehat\Pi_r(A)\) a fixed Borel-measurable sample map for every \(r,n\in\mathbb N\), without requiring \(r\leq n\).
defs.def:estimator:
With the explicit score from \({\rm def:pc-handle}\),
\[
 \widehat\theta_h
 =\frac1n\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}
 \left[q_{i,h}-4\left\{\widehat\Pi_r(A)A
       (Z-\tfrac12\mathbf1_n)\right\}_i\right]Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}.
\]
defs.def:exact-optimal-bandwidth:
At every index for which \(\mathcal H_{n,d}\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\ne\varnothing\), define
\[
 h^\dagger=\min\operatorname*{argmin}_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}
 \mathbb E_P[\overline b_h(A)+\overline s_h(A)].
\]
This is the oracle full-class radius-minimizing bandwidth.  Its evaluation requires the full-class supremum and is not an operational data-driven tuning rule.
defs.def:honest-interval:
Put
\[
 a_\alpha=\sqrt{2\log(2/\alpha)},\qquad
 R_h(A)=\overline b_h(A)+a_\alpha\overline s_h(A),
\]
\[
 L_h=\widehat\theta_h-R_h(A),\qquad
 U_h=\widehat\theta_h+R_h(A),\qquad
 \operatorname{clip}_{[-B,B]}(t)=\max\{-B,\min\{B,t\}\}.
\]
Define the unprojected interval \(\mathcal J_h=[L_h,U_h]\) and the reported interval
\[
 \mathcal C_h=
 [\operatorname{clip}_{[-B,B]}(L_h),
  \operatorname{clip}_{[-B,B]}(U_h)].
\]
Thus \(\mathcal C_h\) is the endpointwise monotone projection of \(\mathcal J_h\) onto the known parameter range.
defs.def:minimax-criteria: At every index for which \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\ne\varnothing\), let \(D=(A,Z,(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}})_{i\in\mathcal V_n})\). Define \(R^*_{n,d,L}=\inf_{\widetilde\theta}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}\mathbb E_P|\widetilde\theta-\theta_n|\), where the infimum ranges over all real-valued measurable estimators \(\widetilde\theta=\widetilde\theta(D)\). Define \(\Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)=\inf_{\mathcal C}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}\mathbb E_P[u(D)-\ell(D)]\), where the infimum ranges over data-measurable closed intervals \(\mathcal C(D)=[\ell(D),u(D)]\) with finite measurable endpoints \(\ell(D)\leq u(D)\) and satisfying \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}P\{\theta_n\in\mathcal C(D)\}\geq1-\alpha\). For every such interval, \(\operatorname{length}\{\mathcal C(D)\}=u(D)-\ell(D)\).
defs.def:model-class: \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}=\{P_{n,d,L}:\text{ every condition in the displayed member-property list holds for }P_{n,d,L}\text{ at triangular-array index }n\}\).  This is the maintained bounded, row-regular, known-rank, two-radius graphon class selected by exactly those properties.  It is neither identified with nor contained in the full Theorem~4/6 regime of LiWager2022RandomGraph; only the intersection of the two regimes is used for comparison.  In particular, \(C_{\log}\log n\leq d\) and \(d/n\to0\) do not imply the source condition \(-1/2<\liminf_n\log(\rho_n)/\log n\), and the displayed member properties do not reproduce every source condition.
defs.def:operational-bandwidth:
At every index for which \(\mathcal H_{n,d}\ne\varnothing\), put \(\ell=d^{-1}\), \(u=\min\{d^{-1/2},1/2\}\), and, for each realized graph \(A\), define the finite nonempty candidate set
\[
 \mathcal K(A)=\{\ell,u\}\cup
 \left\{\left|\frac m{N_i}-\frac12\right|:
 i\in\mathcal V_n,\ N_i>0,\ 0\leq m\leq N_i,\
 \ell\leq\left|\frac m{N_i}-\frac12\right|\leq u\right\}.
\]
The graph-adaptive operational bandwidth is
\[
 \widehat h(A)=\min\operatorname*{argmin}_{h\in\mathcal K(A)}
 \{\overline b_h(A)+\overline s_h(A)\}.
\]
All ties are therefore resolved deterministically toward the smallest candidate.  The construction uses only the observed graph, the known constants, and the finite-lattice certificates; it does not use \(Z\) or the observed outcomes.
defs.def:radii:
For the explicit certificates in \({\rm def:pc-handle}\), set
\[
 \overline b_h(A)=\frac{L}{6n}\sum_{i:N_i>0}h_i(h)^2
 +\frac{B}{n}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}
 +\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}
\]
and
\[
 \overline s_h(A)^2=\widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h}.
\]
Thus \(\overline s_h(A)\) is a finite-sample conditional standard-deviation certificate, not an asserted sharp-rate formula.

assumptions.ass:unit-sampling: \((U_i,f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\) are independent and identically distributed preassignment draws from a joint law whose \(U_i\)-marginal is \({\rm Uniform}[0,1]\).
assumptions.ass:graphon-draw: Conditional on \((U_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\), the variables \((A_{ij})_{i<j}\) are independent with \(A_{ij}\sim{\rm Bernoulli}(\rho_nW(U_i,U_j))\), \(A_{ji}=A_{ij}\), and \(A_{ii}=0\).
assumptions.ass:eigenfunction-bernstein: Each \(\psi_k(U_i)\) satisfies Bernstein's moment condition with parameter \(b_\psi\) for \(1\le k\le r\).

prose_overlay.tldr: A Bernoulli network experiment reveals a derivative only through the exact binomial support associated with each realized degree. The proposal studies the finite-population derivative \(\theta_n\) in the known-rank sparse-graphon model, uses \(h_i(h)=\max\{h,\delta_{N_i}\}\) so every positive degree has a normalized local score, and reports a graph-observable interval radius containing exact degree-level bias, exact inverse score moments, graph dependence, isolates, and feasible-PC remainders. The supported-unit benchmark has lattice, interior, and graph-floor phases. The finite-sample bridge bounds the difference from Li and Wager's finite indirect effect by the displayed degree-exact smoothness and isolate terms, and this difference is \(o_P(\sqrt{\rho_n})\) along maintained sequences in the stated sparsity regime. Li and Wager's equation~(43) is transferred only on the intersection with every source hypothesis and under \(\liminf_n\sigma_{\mathrm{IND},n}>0\); no containment of the maintained class in their theorem is asserted. Because same-class isolate testing gives only the proved \(Bn^{-1}\mathbb E\sqrt{I_0(A)}\) term while the safe interval pays \(Bn^{-1}\mathbb E I_0(A)\), no sharp minimax or honest expected-length frontier is claimed, and a rate-sharp feasible PC construction at logarithmic degree remains open.
prose_overlay.related_work: LiWager2022RandomGraph is the central asymptotic comparator. Its Proposition~1 and equations~(4)--(5) relate its finite indirect effect to an average derivative through a minimum-degree remainder, while its Theorem~6 and equation~(43) give \(\sqrt{\rho_n}\)-scale Gaussian limits under the full source conditions recorded in \({\rm lem:li-wager-theorem-six-regime}\). The present target \(\theta_n\) is the distinct realized finite-population midpoint derivative. Proposition~\({\rm prop:li-wager-bridge}\) proves a degree-exact conditional comparison retaining isolates and proves that the center difference is \(o_P(\sqrt{\rho_n})\) in the stated maintained-class sparsity regime. Transfer of equation~(43) is made only after intersecting with every source hypothesis and imposing \(\liminf_n\sigma_{\mathrm{IND},n}>0\); it is neither a finite-sample equality nor a claim that the maintained class satisfies Li and Wager's theorem. HuLiWager2022AverageDirectIndirect supplies the Bernoulli-policy decomposition and causal interpretation. ArmstrongKolesar2020SimpleHonest informs the computable smoothness-bias interval geometry, while CaiLow2004Adaptation informs the testing-to-expected-length argument; neither treats network support or spectral residualization. AbbeFanWangZhong2020Entrywise and TangCape2025InfiniteRank inform empirical-eigenspace analysis but do not control the exact-support causal score. Leung2022NetworkInference concerns locality-based inference for level effects. BhadraSchweinberger2025Survey is used only as a broad survey of network-interference frameworks.
prose_overlay.interpretation: The supported analytic envelope has three roles: the linear pair gives the graph floor, the local \(C^3\) pair gives the interior smoothness term, and the degree-lattice pair gives the boundary lattice term.  These are minimax lower obstructions and bandwidth geometry.  The reportable interval is nevertheless fully operational and conditionally honest, but its expected length is certified by \(\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}\), not by the supported envelope.
prose_overlay.technical_internal_limitation: The exact score identities control localization bias and expose the bandwidth-free first two Hoeffding projections, but they do not imply a sharp rate for the empirical-projector residual or the bounded-difference variance certificate.  Isolates have no exposure variation: any graph-only conditional-bias radius valid over all supported response configurations must pay \(BI_0(A)/n\), whereas the independent-sign Bayes fluctuation is only of order \(Bn^{-1}\sqrt{I_0(A)}\) conditionally.  Neither fact closes the rate gap between \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\) and \(\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}\).
prose_overlay.honest_scope: The finite-population derivative \(\theta_n\) is the target and is not defined to equal Li and Wager's finite indirect effect. Proposition~\({\rm prop:li-wager-bridge}\) gives their conditional degree-exact separation, including isolates, and proves an \(o_P(\sqrt{\rho_n})\) center approximation along maintained sequences with fixed \(B\) and \(\kappa\) in the stated sparsity regime. LiWager2022RandomGraph Theorem~6 is used only on the further intersection with all of its source hypotheses, with treatment probability one half and \(\liminf_n\sigma_{\mathrm{IND},n}>0\); there is no theorem-wide transfer to every law in \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\) and no transfer to a distinct target. Every positive realized degree is handled by its exact support radius, and isolates remain visible in the certificate. The supported-unit lattice, interior, and graph-floor terms have a lower benchmark, while the conservative feasible envelope is presented only as an upper side of a bracket. A full matched frontier is not claimed because the safe \(Bn^{-1}\mathbb E I_0(A)\) isolate allowance is not matched by the \(Bn^{-1}\mathbb E\sqrt{I_0(A)}\) isolate testing term. A rate-sharp feasible PC construction at logarithmic degree, unknown rank, unknown \(L\), simultaneous policy bands, and optimal ego-cluster design remain outside the proved scope.

project_justification.gap: Li and Wager give asymptotic principal-component inference for a distinct finite indirect effect under their full Theorem~6 regime.  That result does not provide finite-sample conditional coverage or honest expected length for the realized midpoint derivative, and it does not resolve exact low-degree exposure support or isolates.  In the maintained class here, the remaining mathematical gap is a rate-sharp feasible principal-component certificate at logarithmic degree: the proved observable spectral and bounded-difference remainders are finite but have no established comparison with the supported analytic envelope.
project_justification.niche: The paper targets degree-exact estimation and conditional inference for a causal derivative from one sparse graph.  Its distinctive objects are the exact binomial-lattice score, an explicit polynomial-time first-Hoeffding-projection principal-component correction, graph-observable bias and variance radii, and a same-class lower benchmark that separates graph, interior-smoothness, and lattice obstructions.
project_justification.fill: The note proves exact score moments and first two Hoeffding projections, constructs the feasible estimator and a graph-adaptive endpoint-clipped confidence interval with finite-sample conditional coverage, proves the graph-conditional isolate wall, and derives same-class absolute-risk and honest-length lower bounds at the supported envelope.  It combines those lower bounds with the conservative operational upper envelope \(\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}\), explicitly leaving their rate comparison open.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The leading empirical eigenspace of the observed adjacency matrix is used only in the explicit first-projection correction \(q_h-4\widehat\Pi_r(A)A(Z-\mathbf1_n/2)\).  Its graph-observable residualization and coordinate-oscillation certificates are finite and polynomial-time computable; no \(d/n\) rate is asserted for either feasible principal-component remainder.
sampling_model.inference_randomness: Coverage is first conditional on the realized graph and all preassignment response functions, with randomness only from independent Bernoulli assignment; because the selected bandwidth is graph measurable, selection incurs no conditional penalty.  Integrating this guarantee yields uniform honesty over the maintained law class, while the risk and expected-length criteria average over the declared unit, graph, and assignment draws.
sampling_model.units: At each triangular-array index, the preassignment pairs \((U_i,f_i)\) are independent and identically distributed, and the latent-type marginal is exactly \({\rm Uniform}[0,1]\); the finite-population derivative is evaluated after this draw.

lem:exact-score-moments.justification: The exact-support proof establishes positivity, all derivative moment equations, and the third-order Taylor bias with every division justified.

thm:explicit-pc-conditional-certificate.justification: This gives an explicit polynomial-time first-projection PC estimator, an exponential finite-sample conditional certificate, and graph-only selection-valid tuning without asserting the unproved sharp spectral remainder rates. The reported interval projects its ordered endpoints onto \([-B,B]\), so it remains nonempty while preserving the certified coverage event and never increasing length.
thm:explicit-pc-conditional-certificate.gap: No stochastic-order comparison of the empirical-PC bias or bounded-difference variance certificate with the supported analytic envelope is proved.
thm:explicit-pc-conditional-certificate.consumer: Experimenters can compute the graph-adaptive bandwidth and report its selected endpoint-clipped conditional interval; the conservative certificate still transparently marks the unresolved sharp confidence-length rate.

thm:honest-upper.justification: The theorem converts the graph-only finite-breakpoint selector into selection-valid conditional inference and operational integrated guarantees, while retaining the class oracle only as a comparison object. Monotone endpoint clipping preserves coverage because \(\theta_n\in[-B,B]\) and can only shorten the unprojected interval.
thm:honest-upper.gap: The conservative envelope is not proved to have the supported lower-benchmark order.
thm:honest-upper.consumer: Experimenters may report the selected nonempty endpoint-clipped exponential interval directly; its risk and expected length are bounded by the conservative envelope without pretending that envelope is rate sharp.

thm:minimax-lower.gap: The compatibility inequalities are merely sufficient for this explicit block witness and do not characterize nonemptiness. This is a limitation of the witness, not a gap in the supported lower benchmark, which \({\rm thm:unrestricted\text{-}supported\text{-}converse}\) establishes over every eventually nonempty repaired class. The adjacent fixed-known-graph SNIPE frontier is a different estimand, model, and MSE criterion, so it cannot provide a matching upper bound or a converse for the present graphon derivative and closed-interval expected-length criterion. No claim is made for disconnected confidence sets or for the broader adaptation and design-optimization questions treated by the cited comparator classes.
thm:minimax-lower.justification: The explicit equal-block graphon and three same-class response pairs prove the supported analytic converse under the displayed sufficient compatibility conditions. The expected-length reduction applies to uniformly covering closed intervals, whose connectedness turns simultaneous inclusion into a length lower bound; \({\rm thm:unrestricted\text{-}supported\text{-}converse}\) separately proves the same benchmark over every eventually nonempty repaired class. Low1997NonparametricCI is the classical nonparametric honest-CI lower-bound antecedent, whereas this theorem is a same-class one-network graphon lower benchmark rather than an adaptation-impossibility result. The accepted known-graph SNIPE frontier in CausalSmithExpSnipeDegreeFrontierV1 is the closest Bernoulli-network minimax neighbor: it proves a matched design-based MSE frontier for a fixed known directed graph and finite-population total effect over low-order polynomial neighborhood-interference classes. It neither subsumes nor is subsumed by this result: the present theorem averages over a sparse finite-rank graphon law, targets an anonymous-neighbor-fraction midpoint derivative in a local \(C^3\) class, and lower-bounds absolute risk and honest closed-interval expected length, while the SNIPE theorem supplies a matched MSE upper bound in its fixed-graph polynomial setting. KandirosHarshawSavje2026DesignBasedMinimax studies design-based minimax questions on a fixed observed network over designs and arbitrary neighborhood interference; this result fixes Bernoulli assignment and averages over a sparse graphon law for a midpoint derivative. CortezEichhornYu2023LowOrder concerns total effects under low-order polynomial interactions, rather than anonymous treated-neighbor fractions with a local \(C^3\) response class and degree-lattice alternatives. LuLiLiu2026UniformlyBoundedNeighborhood develops bounded-neighborhood asymptotics and adjusted point/variance estimators, whereas the present conclusion is a finite-sample-class minimax lower benchmark for closed-interval expected length and does not supply a matching feasible upper rate.
thm:minimax-lower.consumer: Experimenters may use the supported bandwidth envelope as a certified global lower benchmark for minimax absolute risk and minimax honest expected interval length whenever the repaired class is eventually nonempty; this theorem additionally provides a concrete equal-block witness when its displayed compatibility conditions hold. The accepted SNIPE frontier is an adjacent fixed-graph MSE benchmark, not an optimality certificate for this procedure. This theorem supplies a lower benchmark, not a design-based optimality result, an adaptation theorem, or a matching feasible-PC rate.

thm:conditional-isolate-wall.justification: Opposite derivative signs on realized isolates induce identical conditional observed laws, while the independent-sign submodel gives an exact Rademacher-sum Bayes calculation with lower constant \(B/(\sqrt3\,n)\).
thm:conditional-isolate-wall.gap: The radius conclusion is conditional on the realized graph and response configuration; it does not prove a sharp expected length for every unconditionally honest procedure.
thm:conditional-isolate-wall.consumer: Analysts using the graph-conditional certificate must retain the realized isolate allowance or explicitly adopt a different conditioning convention.

prop:phase-diagram.justification: The phase algebra is unchanged, while the upper bracket is now witnessed by the operational selector with the exponential length constant.
prop:phase-diagram.gap: The lower and upper envelopes remain unlinked, so the bracket may be loose.
prop:phase-diagram.consumer: Use the three phases as tuning geometry and a lower benchmark, not as an achieved minimax or honest-length frontier.

thm:unrestricted-supported-converse.justification: At every sufficiently large nonempty-class index, the proof retains the graph primitives of an arbitrary admissible member and varies only an i.i.d. random-intercept response law.  Uniform conditional-degree bounds then support explicit linear, local \(C^3\)-bump, and degree-lattice two-point experiments.
thm:unrestricted-supported-converse.gap: This theorem settles only the same-class supported lower benchmark.  It supplies no feasible upper comparison and therefore does not identify a sharp minimax or honest expected-length rate.
thm:unrestricted-supported-converse.consumer: The supported analytic envelope is a valid global lower benchmark for every eventually nonempty repaired class, without a null-row modification, an atomic latent-type law, or the equal-block compatibility restrictions.

prop:li-wager-bridge.justification: The bridge separates a maintained-class center approximation from use of the published Gaussian theorem, so the latter is invoked only where every source condition holds.
prop:li-wager-bridge.gap: LiWager2022RandomGraph Proposition~1 gives a minimum-degree approximation; the displayed degree-exact symmetric remainder keeps isolates visible and does not identify the two finite-sample targets. Its Theorem~6 applies only under the full source conditions recorded in the cited lemma.
prop:li-wager-bridge.consumer: It permits asymptotic comparison with Li--Wager equation~(43) only on the stated class intersection while keeping the finite-population derivative as a distinct target everywhere.
